title: Air India Launches Codeshare With Azerbaijan Airlines on Baku-India Routes
excerpt: The new codeshare covers AZAL-operated flights between Baku and both Delhi and Mumbai, upgrading an existing interline agreement as Air India pushes deeper into Central Asia and the Caucasus.
body:
• Air India launched a codeshare with Azerbaijan Airlines (AZAL) on July 29, covering Baku–Delhi and Baku–Mumbai routes operated by AZAL
  • The partnership upgrades an existing interline agreement, allowing Air India to sell tickets on AZAL flights under its own AI code
  • AZAL currently flies to three Indian cities — Delhi, Mumbai, and Ahmedabad — with frequencies increasing to daily on the Mumbai route

Air India has entered a codeshare partnership with Azerbaijan Airlines (AZAL), the Caucasus nation's flag carrier, covering AZAL-operated services between Baku and two major Indian cities. The codeshare routes went live on July 29, according to AeroRoutes.

Under the arrangement, Air India passengers can book AZAL-operated flights on the Baku–Delhi and Baku–Mumbai routes under Air India's marketing code. The flights are operated by AZAL from its hub at Baku's Heydar Aliyev International Airport.

Growing India-Azerbaijan Air Connectivity

AZAL has been steadily expanding its India network. The airline currently operates three weekly flights on the Baku–Delhi route (Mondays, Wednesdays, and Saturdays) and four weekly flights to Mumbai (Tuesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, and Sundays), with the Mumbai service set to increase to daily frequency. In July, AZAL also launched new direct flights to Ahmedabad, its third Indian destination, operating four times a week.

The codeshare upgrade builds on an interline agreement that had already been in place between the two carriers. Wikipedia lists Air India among AZAL's interline partners, and the step up to codeshare status means passengers benefit from seamless booking, coordinated schedules, and through check-in processes.

Air India's Expanding Partnership Network

The AZAL deal is part of Air India's broader strategy to deepen connectivity across Central Asia and the Caucasus through airline partnerships. Since its privatization and takeover by the Tata Group in 2022, Air India has built up 24 codeshare agreements and nearly 100 interline partnerships, according to Safari India, giving customers access to more than 800 destinations worldwide.

"Our new codeshare partnership with Air Astana creates stronger air links to Kazakhstan, a fast-growing market with immense potential for tourism. Beyond serving leisure travel demand, our partnership will also support trade and cultural exchanges between our two countries."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO, Air India (on the earlier Air Astana codeshare)

In 2025, Air India signed a codeshare with Air Astana covering Kazakhstan routes via Almaty, connecting passengers to Astana, Bishkek, Tashkent, Dushanbe, and Urumqi. Earlier in 2026, the airline added Uzbekistan Airways and airBaltic to its codeshare roster. The AZAL partnership continues that trajectory, filling in the Caucasus as Air India extends its reach westward from South Asia.

What It Means for Indian Travelers

For Indian travelers, the codeshare simplifies booking Azerbaijan as a destination. Baku has emerged as a popular travel spot, blending ancient history — its UNESCO-listed Old City — with modern architecture like the Flame Towers. Direct flights from Delhi take roughly four hours, and Mumbai flights around five hours.

AZAL's fares from India remain competitive. One-way economy tickets from Ahmedabad to Baku start around $134, with Mumbai fares from approximately $140 and Delhi fares from $146, based on recent listings on AZAL's website.

The codeshare also opens onward connections through Baku to AZAL's network across Europe, the Middle East, and Central Asia, including destinations like Istanbul, Tbilisi, Prague, and London.

What's Next

The codeshare flights are available for booking through Air India's website, mobile app, and authorized travel agents. Whether the partnership will expand to cover the Ahmedabad route or additional AZAL destinations remains to be seen. With India-Azerbaijan bilateral travel growing and visa-on-arrival available for Indian passport holders, the strengthened air link is well timed for the peak travel season.
